body:
## Summary

- explicitly dispatch the existing release workflow in a non-publishing `validate-pr` mode for release pull requests created with `GITHUB_TOKEN`
- wait for that exact validation run to succeed before attempting the ruleset-protected merge, and abort without merging when validation fails
- preserve least privilege with job-scoped `actions: write`, keep validation preflight in report mode, and cover both automatic and instant release paths through the shared landing helper
- add a failing-first regression, update all four CI/CD best-practice translations, and include the required patch changeset

## Root cause and reproduction

At 2026-09-20 04:28:10 UTC, the main ruleset began strictly requiring `Pipeline Status`. The existing fallback opened its release PR with `GITHUB_TOKEN`; GitHub left the ordinary `pull_request` workflows in `action_required`, so no `Pipeline Status` check was ever created. Ten merge retries could only repeat the invariant policy failure.

This reproduced in four consecutive main runs, creating release PRs #2268, #2272, #2273, and #2276. All twelve workflows attached to those PRs are `action_required`.

Before this change:

1. direct version push is rejected by the ruleset
2. fallback release PR is created
3. required check never starts
4. all merge attempts fail with `Required status check "Pipeline Status" is expected`

After this change, the fallback dispatches `release.yml` on the generated head with `release_mode=validate-pr`, watches the returned run with `--exit-status`, and reaches merge only after successful validation. Publication jobs remain restricted to a push on `main` or explicit `instant` mode.

## Verification

- final evidence head `63f2f24f` — [Checks and release](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/35529722059), [Security](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/35529721830), [Workflows](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/35529721877), and [Broken Link Checker](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/35529721810) all passed
- implementation candidate `1e1de488` — all four workflows passed, including full Docker/container validation; its complete logs are archived in the evidence bundle
- `npm test` — all 495 selected test files passed
- `node scripts/run-tests.mjs --suite github-integration` — selected integration file passed, 4/4 assertions
- `npm run lint`
- `npm run format:check`
- `npm run check:duplication`
- `npm run check:secrets`
- `node tests/extracted-modules-2198.test.mjs`
- `bash scripts/check-file-line-limits.sh` — `release.yml` is 1,348 lines
- issue #2274 regression verifies validation-before-merge and proves failed validation never calls merge

## Evidence and related project

The complete investigation is archived in [`dev/log/issues/2274/pulls/2275`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/tree/issue-2274-beb53fa7caf4/dev/log/issues/2274/pulls/2275), including the timeline, every requirement, root-cause/solution matrix, eight full CI logs, ruleset version history, annotation audit, template file/checksum comparison, local test logs, and primary-source research.

The same defect exists in the upstream JavaScript CI/CD template and is reported with reproductions, workarounds, and a code-level fix plan in link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#192.

Fixes #2274
title: Fix required-check deadlock in automated releases

body:
## Summary

- add a fail-closed, repository-wide dependency freshness inventory and run it before release change detection
- configure daily grouped Dependabot updates for npm, Actions, Docker, Compose, and Helm
- update all 17 stale declarations found in the initial 138-record scan and expand coverage to 148 declarations
- refresh six safe operational CLIs in long-lived containers through the existing idle-only updater
- preserve the investigation, upstream release logs, registry evidence, reports, and ruleset snapshots in a case study

Fixes #2264.

## Root cause

The reported `gh-upload-log` contradiction combined three issues: its version was hard-coded, GitHub release 0.9.0 existed even though npm publication failed, and running containers had no update path for operational CLIs. More broadly, dependency declarations were split among manifests, `use-m` maps, Dockerfiles, workflows, setup inputs, base images, and embedded binaries with no common freshness postcondition.

The upstream publication path was independently corrected in link-foundation/gh-upload-log#41 and npm now serves 0.9.1. This investigation also reported the residual formatter false-success as link-foundation/gh-upload-log#43 and the broken published `gh-load-issue@0.3.2` entry point as link-foundation/gh-load-issue#18.

## Implementation

- `scripts/check-dependency-freshness.mjs` resolves stable npm and GitHub releases with retries, deduplication, precision-aware policies, and fail-closed errors.
- The required `detect-changes` job runs freshness first, while `Pipeline Status` observes the result.
- `.github/dependabot.yml` proposes one daily multi-ecosystem update. All five ecosystems explicitly opt out of GitHub's default three-day cooldown so automated remediation agrees with the immediate freshness gate; the scoped zizmor exception documents that decision.
- Main ruleset 7927725 now strictly requires the GitHub Actions `Pipeline Status` context. The existing deletion, non-fast-forward, and pull-request rules were preserved, and before/after API snapshots are committed with the investigation.
- The idle updater now includes `claude-profiles`, `gh-setup-git-identity`, `gh-pull-all`, `gh-load-issue`, `gh-load-pull-request`, and `gh-upload-log` while preserving its active-task guard, process lock, throttle, allow/deny lists, and per-tool isolation.
- Broken `--version` entry points fall back to `bun pm ls -g`, allowing an installed package to remain maintainable without masking the upstream executable defect.
- `command-stream` 0.24.1 activates the quote-context fix introduced in 0.20.0; the issue #2119 regression now proves quoted and bare interpolations both preserve exact arguments.

## Reproduction and verification

Before the fix, the archived scan found 17 stale declarations (`121/138` current). The final live scan reports `148/148` current.

- `npx --yes --package npm@11.19.1 -- npm test` — all 491 selected test files passed
- `npm run lint`
- `npm run format:check`
- `npm run check:duplication`
- `npm run check:secrets`
- `npm audit --audit-level=low` — 0 vulnerabilities
- `node scripts/check-dependency-freshness.mjs` — 148/148 current
- actionlint 1.7.12 and Helm 4.3 lint checks passed against the updated workflow/chart inputs

The complete implementation run passed the 491-file suite, both production image builds, and in-container tool verification before the status was made required: [Checks and release 35488145037](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/35488145037). The final evidence head `88550346` is also fully green:

- [Checks and release 35489282414](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/35489282414), including the required [`Pipeline Status`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/35489282414/job/106021542087)
- [Security 35489282253](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/35489282253)
- [Workflows 35489282241](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/35489282241)
- [Broken Link Checker 35489282243](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/35489282243)

The new regression uses a mocked registry for deterministic stale/current/error cases, inventories the real repository, verifies workflow and Dependabot wiring, simulates the `gh-upload-log` 0.1.0-to-0.9.1 transition, and proves a broken executable can still be refreshed from package-manager metadata.

## Evidence

See [`docs/case-studies/issue-2264`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/tree/issue-2264-0a04b3d4fcdc/docs/case-studies/issue-2264) for the timeline, root-cause analysis, full evidence index, upstream reports, and compressed workflow logs.

This is a non-visual CI/runtime maintenance change, so screenshots are not applicable.
title: Enforce dependency freshness across CI and running containers

body:
Closes #2279.

## What failed

The automated release fallback opened a protected-branch PR with
`GITHUB_TOKEN`. Its ordinary `pull_request` workflows stayed
`action_required`, so the required `Pipeline Status` check never appeared.
The #2274 workaround dispatched `release.yml` manually and that run passed on
the exact PR SHA, but GitHub does not evaluate `workflow_dispatch` job checks
as pull-request required checks. Runs 35530983182 and 35536619299 were therefore
green while release PRs #2277 and #2278 still had empty check rollups and could
not merge.

The auto-restart run then exposed a separate valid freshness failure:
command-stream 0.25.0 was published after the preceding detector had passed,
leaving the exact 0.24.1 runtime pin stale. During final local verification,
use-m 8.16.1 was likewise published after an earlier 148/148 freshness result.

## What changed

- Open fallback release PRs through a dedicated independent token and wait for
  the checks associated with the PR via `gh pr checks --watch`.
- Remove the ineligible `validate-pr` dispatch mode and its `actions: write`
  permission.
- Fail before creating an orphan release branch when the independent token is
  absent.
- Retry only the short check-discovery/mergeability races; propagate permanent
  required-check, review, and base-policy failures immediately.
- Correct the prior #2274 regression and add pre-fix coverage for #2279 across
  both release modes.
- Refresh yargs 18.1.0 to 18.2.0, command-stream 0.24.1 to 0.25.0, and both
  immutable use-m bootstrap URLs from 8.16.0 to 8.16.1, with their live pin
  contracts and install/specifier assertions.
- Suppress the intentional legacy-entry-point deprecation only in the
  auto-fork compatibility test, while retaining the dedicated deprecation
  regression.
- Pin all 35 active Linux jobs and matrix entries to Ubuntu 24.04 after fresh
  CI warned that `ubuntu-latest` will migrate to Ubuntu 26 in October 2026.
- Update all four CI/CD best-practice translations and add the required patch
  changeset.

## Reproduction and verification

The production sequence and complete issue/PR/run/ruleset evidence are under
[`dev/log/issues/2279/pulls/2280`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/tree/issue-2279-b1afd26393ba/dev/log/issues/2279/pulls/2280).
`tests/release-required-checks-2279.test.mjs` was committed first and failed on
the old implementation because it dispatched a workflow instead of waiting on
PR-associated checks. The evidence bundle also contains the exact auto-restart
failure, the preceding green run, npm publication timestamps, upstream source
comparisons, focused before/after logs, and a verified SHA-256 manifest.

Verified locally on head `6a1301c1`:

- complete default suite: 499/499 test files passed;
- live GitHub integration suite: 4/4 assertions passed;
- authenticated dependency freshness immediately before push: 148/148;
- focused #2175, #2274, and #2279 release regressions;
- changeset validation against the exact PR base/head and the active-workflow
  runner-image regression;
- actionlint, status gate, Changesets guards, syntax, line limits, ESLint,
  Prettier, duplication, secretlint, full-PR `git diff --check`, and
  compatibility checks.

Verified by GitHub on exact head `6a1301c135a28557b05fa89d7e99b1b0887a0fbe`:

- [Checks and release run 35584857795](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/35584857795): passed, including `detect-changes`, the complete test suite, Docker validation, and required `Pipeline Status`;
- [Security run 35584857327](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/35584857327): passed;
- [Workflows run 35584857291](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/35584857291): passed;
- [Broken Link Checker run 35584857249](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/35584857249): passed;
- no warning or failure annotations; the link check's sole annotation is its informational summary notice.

This is not a UI change, so screenshots are not applicable.

## Required administrator action

Before the next protected-branch release, add a repository Actions secret named
`RELEASE_PULL_REQUEST_TOKEN` containing a dedicated, repository-scoped
fine-grained PAT with only the permissions needed to read Actions/check state,
create and merge pull requests, and update repository contents. A custom
GitHub App installation token is the preferred short-lived follow-up and can
be wired to the same step-local `GH_TOKEN` interface.

The matching defect in the upstream pipeline template is documented with a
minimal reproduction, workarounds, and corrected implementation plan in
[link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#192](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/192#issuecomment-5756981358).
The template's 33 mutable Ubuntu aliases are separately reported in
[template issue #193](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/193).

body:
## Summary

Fixes #2175: a full sweep of the CI/CD annotations on the failing default-branch run [`32589574378`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/32589574378) and its green predecessors. Every error and every warning those runs emitted is now gone, and the two false negatives that let a broken release look healthy are closed.

The complete investigation — evidence, timeline, root cause per defect, template comparison and verification map — is committed alongside the fix in [`dev/log/issues/2175/pulls/2176/ANALYSIS.md`](dev/log/issues/2175/pulls/2176/ANALYSIS.md), with the raw logs and API captures beside it.

## What was wrong, and why

### 1. Error — the release job could not succeed at all (GH013)

At 17:34 UTC a `pull_request` rule with an **empty bypass list** was added to the Main ruleset. From that moment `GITHUB_TOKEN` may not push to `main`, so the 18:11 release run was rejected:

```
remote: error: GH013: Repository rule violations found for refs/heads/main.
remote: - Changes must be made through a pull request.
 ! [remote rejected]   main -> main (push declined due to repository rule violations)
```

`2.13.5` was committed in the runner and never published. This is **not** a lost race, so the existing rebase-and-retry recovery (issue #2082) could never fix it.

**Fix.** `scripts/release-pull-request.lib.mjs` classifies the rejection and lands the same version commit through a pull request: push to a run-scoped branch, `gh pr create`, `gh pr merge --merge` (retried while GitHub computes mergeability), then fast-forward the local checkout so npm publish, the GitHub release, Docker and Helm all run against the merged tree. `isNonFastForward` now explicitly returns `false` for a rule violation so it can never be retried as a race. The branch is never force-pushed and never deleted (`no-destruction-possible` targets `~ALL`) and the merge method is `merge` (`allowed_merge_methods: ["merge"]`). The bot e-mail was also corrected to `41898282+github-actions[bot]@…` — without the numeric prefix the commit is unattributed and `require_extra_approval_for_unattributed_changes` would block the merge on a human approval.

### 2. False negative — changesets were the release oracle

The release steps were gated on "does `.changeset` contain any `*.md`?", which cannot distinguish *nothing to do* from *a version bump landed but was never published* — the exact state an interrupted release leaves behind, and one with no failing check anywhere.

**Fix.** `scripts/check-release-needed.mjs` asks the **npm registry**, the source of truth for "is this released?". No changesets + version missing from npm ⇒ `should_release=true`, `skip_bump=true`, publish what is already committed. This mirrors the template's own `check-release-needed.mjs`.

### 3. Warning — Node 20 deprecation

`softprops/action-gh-release@v2` is pinned to the deprecated Node 20 runtime. Replaced by `scripts/upload-release-assets.sh` using `gh release upload`; the template has no reference to that action either.

### 4. Warnings — eight files in the 1350-line band

Each was reduced by extracting a cohesive module with injected dependencies (the issue #2150 §6 pattern), re-exporting every moved symbol so importers and tests are unaffected:

| File | Before | After | Extracted module |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `src/hive.mjs` | 1465 | 1323 | `hive.repository-fallback.lib.mjs`, `hive.startup-checks.lib.mjs` |
| `src/session-monitor.lib.mjs` | 1416 | 1156 | `session-monitor.queries.lib.mjs` |
| `src/claude.lib.mjs` | 1401 | 1247 | `claude.session-tokens.lib.mjs` |
| `src/solve.mjs` | 1398 | 1248 | `solve.mode.lib.mjs` |
| `src/telegram-solve-queue.lib.mjs` | 1374 | 1121 | `telegram-solve-queue.throttling.lib.mjs` |
| `src/codex.lib.mjs` | 1367 | 1250 | `codex.diagnostics.lib.mjs` |
| `src/solve.auto-pr.lib.mjs` | 1361 | 1225 | `solve.auto-pr-push-sync.lib.mjs` |
| `src/isolation-runner.lib.mjs` | 1357 | 1084 | `isolation-runner.parsers.lib.mjs` |

`bash scripts/check-file-line-limits.sh` now reports no "approaching" files. One extraction also removed an accidental lint exemption: the auto-continue fork check now goes through `githubLib.ghPrView` instead of a direct `gh` call.

### 5. False positives

None found. The analysis records the two candidate classes examined and why each annotation was a true positive.

## How to reproduce the original failure

1. Add a ruleset on `main` with **Require a pull request before merging** and an empty bypass list.
2. Merge any pull request carrying a changeset.
3. The release job fails in "Version packages and commit to main" with the GH013 output above.

## Tests

- `tests/release-pull-request-2175.test.mjs` — classification of the verbatim GH013 output, run-scoped branch naming, merge retry while mergeability is unknown, and the end-to-end fallback from a rejected push.
- `tests/check-release-needed-2175.test.mjs` — all four release-gate states plus the exact output strings `if:` expressions compare against.
- `tests/hive-extracted-modules-2175.test.mjs` — behaviour of the extracted modules.
- Four source-level tests were updated to read the module that now holds the code they assert on (`test-issue-1829-compare-api-transient`, `test-issue-1716-private-repo-skip-fork`, `test-issue-1332-fork-name-from-pr-data`, `test-owner-fork-detection`).
- Seven test files now read module sources with `readFileSync` instead of `execSync(\`cat ...\`)`; all seven suites pass with the same assertion counts as before.
- `solve.mjs` was smoke-tested end to end with `--dry-run` against both an issue URL and a PR URL.

## CodeQL

The code-scanning gate on this pull request reported 14 new alerts (2 high, 12 medium). Both groups are fixed at the root rather than suppressed; the annotations are archived in `dev/log/issues/2175/pulls/2176/codeql/annotations.json` and analysed in `ANALYSIS.md`.

- **12 medium** — `Unnecessary use of 'cat' process` and `Shell command built from environment values`, raised against `execSync(\`cat ${srcDir}/<module>.mjs\`)` in the test suite. The pattern predates this PR, but the extractions rewrote those exact lines, so CodeQL saw them as new. Replaced with `readFileSync(path, 'utf8')` — CodeQL's own suggested fix — across all 55 occurrences in seven files, plus the one `grep -l` shell-out of the same shape that was only unflagged because its line happened to be untouched. `execSync` is now unused in those files and its import was dropped.
- **2 high** — `Incomplete URL substring sanitization` and `Incomplete string escaping or encoding` inside `dev/log/.../template-scripts/`. Those are verbatim copies of the upstream template scripts collected as evidence; this repository never executes them and cannot fix them. Added `.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml` with `paths-ignore: dev/log`, wired into both matrix legs, matching how the same directory is already excluded from Prettier and jscpd.

## Upstream reports

Both defects reproduce in the CI/CD template at its current `main`, so they were reported there with reproducers, workarounds and code-level fixes:

- link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#143 — rebase-retry cannot land a push blocked by a `pull_request` ruleset.
- link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#144 — release commits are unattributed (bot e-mail missing the `41898282+` prefix).

## Known gap, recorded not hidden

Seven test files fail on an unmodified checkout but are excluded from CI by the `@hive-mind-test-suite needs-triage` tag. Each was verified to fail identically on a stashed tree, so none is caused by this PR. They are a genuine CI blind spot and are listed in the analysis; triaging seven unrelated product failures belongs in their own issues rather than in a CI/CD remediation PR.

Fixes #2175
title: Fix all CI/CD errors, warnings and release false negatives (issue #2175)

body:
Fixes #2164

## Summary

By default a Docker-isolated task is handed the operator's real subscription: `~/.claude`, `~/.claude.json`, `~/.codex`, `~/.agents` and `~/.config/gh` are bind-mounted into the container. The agent inside holds the raw vendor OAuth credential, can spend the subscription without limit, and leaves no record of what it did beyond what it chose to write itself.

`--use-router` (**experimental**) withholds those mounts. The credentials stay in a single reference-counted `hive-mind-router` sidecar on an internal Docker network, each task is joined to that network and given its own `la_sk_…` token scoped to the one repository it works on, and every model request lands in that token's own redacted log.

```bash
solve https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/42 --isolation docker --use-router
```

Nothing changes without the flag — that is deliberate (R9): this is opt-in isolation, not a migration.

Every requirement was analysed against first-party evidence before any code was written; the analysis, the pinned upstream sources and the checksummed evidence set are in [`docs/case-studies/issue-2164/`](docs/case-studies/issue-2164/README.md).

## Upstream first (R16), and what it unblocked

The audit of router `v0.105.0` found four gaps, and per the issue they were reported upstream before any workaround was written here: [router#260](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/260) (stored OpenAI-compatible providers ignored by automatic routing), [#261](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/261) (git transport bypasses the policy engine), [#262](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/262) (per-deployment GitHub credential and policy), [#263](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/263) (no TLS listener, so `gh` cannot use the router as a host).

**All four were fixed upstream on 2026-08-21** and shipped in `v0.106.0`–`v0.109.0`. This PR pins `ghcr.io/link-assistant/router:0.119.0`, which is what makes R11, R12 and the transport half of R13 deliverable here rather than deferred. Re-measuring produced three further upstream reports — [#270](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/270), [#271](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/271), [#272](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/272) — **all three since fixed**. A re-audit against `v0.119.0` on 2026-08-26 filed four more: [#322](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/322), [#323](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/323), [#324](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/324) (fixed; #323 partially — tier aliases declined by design) and [#329](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/329), which is the one remaining limit (see [Limits](#what-is-not-covered)).

## What changed

| #           | Requirement                              | Delivered by                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| R1, R9, R10 | The flag, opt-in, marked experimental    | `--use-router` in `SOLVE_OPTION_DEFINITIONS` with the `[EXPERIMENTAL]` prefix; `HIVE_MIND_USE_ROUTER=1` carries the decision into the bot and nested runs                                                                           |
| R2, R3      | Router is the only point of contact      | `src/router-isolation.lib.mjs` suppresses the credential mounts at the seam in `src/isolation-runner.lib.mjs`; the sidecar alone mounts the subscription                                                                            |
| R4          | Verify the router actually supports this | Part 2 of the case study, quoted against the pinned router README, then re-measured against `v0.109.0` in `docs/case-studies/issue-2164/data/measurements/`                                                                        |
| R5          | Run only while a task needs it           | Lease-counted sidecar in `src/router-sidecar.lib.mjs`; the bot's maintenance tick reconciles leases against Docker and stops idle routers                                                                                           |
| R6          | One token per task, one log per task     | One `router tokens issue` per session id, scoped with `--github-repo`, revoked on release, never shared                                                                                                                             |
| R7          | Merge session data back at end of task   | `src/router-session-drain.lib.mjs` — `docker cp` works on stopped containers, so a crashed task is drained as well as a clean one                                                                                                   |
| R8, R14     | Keep the logs, make them readable        | Named volume `hive-mind-router-data` that **no code path removes**; `src/router-logs.lib.mjs` reads it with or without a running router                                                                                             |
| R11         | `--model formal-ai` through the router   | `registerFormalAiWithRouter()` stores the Formal AI sidecar as an OpenAI-compatible provider (`router providers add`); the router dispatches on the model id, so other tasks are unaffected                                         |
| R12         | Route `gh` and `git`                     | The sidecar terminates TLS with a certificate naming `api.github.com`, the task resolves that host to the router, and each client is handed the CA the way it expects (`NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, `SSL_CERT_FILE`, `CURL_CA_BUNDLE`, `http.<url>.sslCAInfo`). An unmodified `gh` is mediated and the task holds no GitHub credential |
| R13         | Block destructive git operations         | Three layers: branch protection; a read-only `pre-push` hook (`src/git-push-guard.lib.mjs`); and the router's `/git/*` transport, which refuses ref deletions with HTTP 403 (measured in `data/measurements/git-transport.log`) and, from router `0.110.0`, non-fast-forward updates as well. The gh-API half is partial — see Limits |
| R15         | Document log collection system-wide      | [`docs/COLLECTING-LOGS.md`](docs/COLLECTING-LOGS.md) ×4 languages and `examples/collect-logs.mjs`, both driven by one `describeSystemLogLocations()`                                                                                |
| R16         | Report upstream gaps first               | router#260–#263 filed before the corresponding code; #270–#272 filed after re-measuring `v0.109.0` (all fixed); #322, #323, #324, #329 filed in the 2026-08-26 re-audit of `v0.119.0`                                                                                                                                  |
| R17         | Case study                               | [`docs/case-studies/issue-2164/`](docs/case-studies/issue-2164/README.md) with a checksummed `MANIFEST.md` and the raw probe logs                                                                                                   |

Along the way, `src/docker-sidecar.lib.mjs` extracts the container lifecycle both sidecars share, and `src/formal-ai-sidecar.lib.mjs` is rewritten on top of it — same behaviour, one implementation.

The signing secret never enters a task's environment, is never logged, and `examples/collect-logs.mjs` deliberately refuses to copy the state directory into an evidence archive.

## What is *not* covered

These limits are documented in [`docs/ROUTER.md`](docs/ROUTER.md) **and printed before every routed run**, so nobody discovers them by being breached:

- **Destructive GitHub API calls are blocked by method, not by effect** — [router#329](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/329). Every `DELETE`, forced REST ref update and destructive GraphQL mutation is refused. The same outcomes spelled differently are not: `PUT /repos/{o}/{r}/branches/{b}/protection` replaces a protection object wholesale, `PUT .../rulesets/{id}` relaxes a ruleset, `POST .../transfer` moves the repository, and `PATCH /repos/{o}/{r}` can flip `visibility`, `archived` or `default_branch`. Branch protection is reachable this way, so it is a strong default rather than a control a routed task cannot touch. Bounded in practice by the permissions of the `gh` credential the router presents upstream.
- **A force push _is_ now blocked**, contrary to what earlier revisions of this PR said. [router#272](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/272) was fixed in [router#273](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/pull/273) and shipped in `v0.110.0`, seventeen minutes after the comment here describing it as open. The router asks GitHub's compare API whether the proposed tip is ahead of the current one and fails closed when it cannot tell.
- **The Formal AI sidecar's own upstream calls are not routed.** `--model formal-ai` reaches Formal AI through the router, but if that server itself calls a vendor API, that leg leaves the sidecar directly.
- **Non-Claude tools are less exercised.** codex, gemini and qwen are wired through the router's OpenAI-compatible surface; only Claude Code has an end-to-end probe in `experiments/issue-2164/`.
- **Model aliases are rejected** — the router ships no alias table by design ([router#192](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/192)) and declined to add tier resolution ([router#323](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/323)), so `--model claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929` works where `--model sonnet` does not. Since `0.115.0` the refusal lists the ids that would have worked. This affects the tier-shaped surface generally — `--plan`, `--escalate` and the fallback chains all name tiers — so pin dated ids on a routed run. The remedy is on our side (export `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL` resolved from `GET /v1/models`) and is deliberately left out of this PR pending a measurement; see the case study's re-audit section.
- **`HIVE_MIND_ROUTER_GITHUB=0`, or an external router**, leaves the task with its own `gh` credential; an external router has no container network of ours to intercept in and needs `HIVE_MIND_ROUTER_GH_HOST`.

## Tests

Five regression suites, all in the default suite and all passing locally, alongside `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check` and `npm run check:duplication`:

| Suite                                        | What it pins down                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `tests/test-issue-2164-router-isolation.mjs` | Credentials are actually suppressed when routed and untouched when not; GitHub interception, CA trust and the git routing config are wired as documented; every coverage gap is warned about      |
| `tests/test-issue-2164-router-sidecar.mjs`   | Lease counting, idle stop, launch grace, one repo-scoped token per task, the Formal AI provider registration (R11), and that the signing secret never reaches a task                                                                                      |
| `tests/test-issue-2164-session-drain.mjs`    | Session data is archived before the token is revoked, including from stopped containers                                                                                                                       |
| `tests/test-issue-2164-log-collection.mjs`   | The logs are still readable after the sidecar is gone, collection cannot damage what it collects, and the docs list matches the code's list                                                                    |
| `tests/test-issue-2164-git-push-guard.mjs`   | Runs the hook against a **real repository and a real remote**: force-push after `git reset --hard` and `push --delete` both fail, the remote still holds the discarded commit, an ordinary push still succeeds |

Behaviour that only a live router can show — TLS interception, the git transport's 403, the Formal AI provider — is recorded as raw probe output in [`docs/case-studies/issue-2164/data/measurements/`](docs/case-studies/issue-2164/data/measurements/), with the probe scripts kept in `experiments/issue-2164/`.
